# City2Graph

> City2Graph is a Python library for constructing spatial and heterogeneous
> graphs from buildings, streets, public transport feeds, origin–destination
> matrices, zones, and points of interest. It connects GeoPandas, NetworkX,
> rustworkx, and PyTorch Geometric for spatial network analysis and Graph Neural
> Networks.

City2Graph documentation is written for geospatial developers, data scientists,
and urban, mobility, and transport researchers. The links below point to the
latest documentation.

## Start here

- [Overview](https://city2graph.net/latest/index.html): Capabilities, supported data, workflow guide, quickstart, and frequently asked questions.
- [Open-access paper](https://city2graph.net/latest/paper.html): Author-written abstract, complete citation metadata, DOI, licence, and links to the Version of Record.
- [Version of Record PDF](https://city2graph.net/latest/assets/papers/sato2026city2graph.pdf): Open-access publisher PDF under the CC BY 4.0 licence.
- [Installation](https://city2graph.net/latest/installation.html): pip, conda-forge, PyTorch CPU, and supported CUDA installation options.
- [Tutorials](https://city2graph.net/latest/examples/index.html): Task-oriented notebooks and applied projects.
- [Python API reference](https://city2graph.net/latest/api/index.html): Public modules and functions organised by task.

## Research paper

**Title:** City2Graph: A Python library for Heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks
and spatial analysis in urban systems

**Authors:** Yuta Sato, Elisabetta Pietrostefani, Ron Mahabir, and Daniel
Arribas-Bel

**Publication:** *Computers, Environment and Urban Systems*, volume 130,
article 102492 (2026)

**DOI:** [10.1016/j.compenvurbsys.2026.102492](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compenvurbsys.2026.102492)

**Abstract:** City2Graph is an open-source Python library that streamlines
workflows for heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) in urban systems.
Cities are complex systems of diverse spatial relations long modelled as graphs
in network science, and recent advances in GNNs have further enabled the
identification of non-linear patterns of urban complexity. Unlike homogeneous
graphs with a single node and edge type, heterogeneous graphs with multiple
types are receiving growing attention to accommodate richer information in
GNNs. However, their diffusion remains constrained by fragmented graph
construction processes across different data domains, and by the lack of a
unified framework for converting constructed graphs into GNN-ready tensors.
City2Graph standardises graph construction across domains of morphology,
transportation, mobility, and proximity. The library supports conversions
between spatial geometries, network topologies, and tensors for spatial analysis
with visualisation, network analysis, and GNN training, respectively. City2Graph
also supports metapath construction, capturing higher-order connections across
node and edge types (e.g., areas linked via multimodal transit). The library’s
efficacy was demonstrated through a case study on clustering urban functions in
Liverpool, UK, using Graph Autoencoder models with three relation types: spatial
contiguity, walk-based accessibility, and multimodal accessibility between
census units. Compared with the homogeneous model, heterogeneous models
identified spatially coherent clusters that aligned more closely with defined
accessibility patterns. City2Graph enables reproducible workflows for
heterogeneous GNNs and model interpretation, fostering comprehensive
understanding of urban systems across disciplines. The library is released
under the BSD 3-Clause License on GitHub.

- [Paper landing page](https://city2graph.net/latest/paper.html)
- [Direct PDF](https://city2graph.net/latest/assets/papers/sato2026city2graph.pdf)
- [Formal publication on ScienceDirect](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0198971526000943)
- [CC BY 4.0 licence](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

## Tutorials

- [Urban morphology from Overture Maps and OpenStreetMap](https://city2graph.net/latest/examples/morphological_graph_from_overturemaps.html): Build heterogeneous graphs from buildings, tessellations, and streets.
- [GTFS public transport graphs](https://city2graph.net/latest/examples/gtfs.html): Build stop-to-stop travel-time graphs and multimodal isochrones.
- [OD matrices and mobility graphs](https://city2graph.net/latest/examples/generating_graphs_from_od_matrix.html): Convert edge lists and adjacency matrices into weighted spatial graphs.
- [Spatial proximity graphs](https://city2graph.net/latest/examples/generating_graphs_by_proximity.html): Construct KNN, Delaunay, Gilbert, Waxman, and contiguity graphs.
- [Metapaths for heterogeneous GNNs](https://city2graph.net/latest/examples/add_metapaths.html): Add composite typed relations to heterogeneous graphs.

## API modules

- [Graph conversion](https://city2graph.net/latest/api/graph.html): Convert between GeoDataFrames, NetworkX, and PyTorch Geometric.
- [Data](https://city2graph.net/latest/api/data.html): Load Overture Maps data and place boundaries.
- [Morphology](https://city2graph.net/latest/api/morphology.html): Build building, tessellation, and street relations.
- [Transportation](https://city2graph.net/latest/api/transportation.html): Load GTFS or GBFS data and build travel-summary graphs.
- [Mobility](https://city2graph.net/latest/api/mobility.html): Convert origin–destination data to weighted graphs.
- [Proximity](https://city2graph.net/latest/api/proximity.html): Build proximity, contiguity, bridge, grouping, and directed graphs.
- [Metapath](https://city2graph.net/latest/api/metapath.html): Materialise metapath-derived relations.

## Project

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/c2g-dev/city2graph): Source code, issues, releases, and contribution workflow.
- [PyPI package](https://pypi.org/project/city2graph/): Python package releases and installation metadata.
- [Journal article](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compenvurbsys.2026.102492): Sato, Pietrostefani, Mahabir, and Arribas-Bel (2026), Computers, Environment and Urban Systems 130, 102492. Citing this paper is required when City2Graph is used in research.
- [Citation metadata](https://github.com/c2g-dev/city2graph/blob/main/CITATION.cff): Citation File Format record.
